title: Where this colony's food comes from, and how it moves
question: With it on (B), can you tell where the food is coming from and which way it travels?
context_md:
New view in the lab, **`F7`** (off / food road / harvest map / both). Same bed, same 5,600 frames, scrub the two together.

- **amber hatch** — ground the colony has taken food out of, in that colony's own colour, brighter and denser the more it has given up. It fades over about a minute of play, so it is where they are working *now*, not everywhere they have ever been.
- **red-orange line** — an ant walked here **carrying**. White-hot where the traffic is heaviest.
- **blue line** — an ant walked here with nothing.

The hatch is deliberately see-through: painted solid it covered the very plants it was pointing at.

**What I am unsure of and would rather you judged than I did:** whether the amber reads as *ground that fed them* or just as a stain over the plants, and whether the blue is useful context or clutter. It ships off by default.

items.label: A — as the lab looks today
items.caption: the control: same world, same frames, nothing drawn over it

items.label: B — F7, road + harvest
items.caption: amber = ground they took food from; red-orange = walked carrying; blue = walked empty

meta.extra time per frame with this on: +1.6 ms of 3.9 while things move, +1.7 of 2.0 once they stop
